# Boundary stress does not propagate a deepest marked stratum

This note tests an exact interface, not the mixed-integer conjecture. The normal-preserving martingale obtained from all convex-potential tests acts on actual fiber BOUNDARIES. The physical retained-mass and projective-energy strata consist of INTERIOR deepest points. Equality on the boundary does not transfer the latter status to destination fibers.

The distinction persists for an actual globally critical cap circuit, a unique deepest mixed point, and every strict proper-closed-minor count quota. The examples below have depth far above the conjectured lower bound. They do not test the additional hypothesis of an attained strict bad-depth minimum.

## 1. What exact convex equality really implies

Let pi be a finite martingale coupling of compact measures nu to eta in R^m. Thus its conditional law pi_w has mean w for nu-almost every w. If a finite continuous convex function Phi satisfies

    integral Phi dnu=integral Phi deta,                         (1)

then, for nu-almost every w and EVERY subgradient a of Phi at w,

    Phi(w')=Phi(w)+a dot (w'-w)  for pi_w-almost every w'.      (2)

Proof: conditional Jensen gives integral Phi dpi_w-Phi(w)>=0. Its integral is zero by (1), so the conditional gap is zero almost everywhere. For any fixed such w and any a in the subdifferential, the nonnegative supporting-plane gap has integral zero, proving (2). No measurable subgradient selection is needed for this rowwise conclusion. For finitely or countably many functions satisfying (1), intersect their full-measure sets.

Thus equality confines transport to common affine contact sets of the tested functions. If Phi is strictly convex, those sets are singletons, so pi is diagonal and nu=eta. If Phi>=0 vanishes precisely on a closed convex set D, a source row AT A POINT OF D whose Jensen gap is zero has its entire target law in D. This is a valid sufficient condition for support transfer.

Neither condition is automatic for the actual boundary stress. The proved stress inequalities are

    integral Phi dnu<=integral Phi deta

for convex Phi, with equality for signed affine tests. They do not give equality for strictly convex Phi. A boundary source point does not belong to the positive-depth superlevel set D. In actual compatible fibers every own-boundary point has mixed depth zero, by the supporting-affine-roof argument in the archived deepest-stratum theorem.

The following lemma is also useful when attempting to insert fiber invariants. For fixed K, extend T_K and E_K by zero to its boundary. These extensions are continuous. For T, take any approaching sequence of marks and weak-* limits of the optimizing densities 0<=f<=1_K. A limiting boundary barycenter forces the density onto a null supporting hyperplane, so the retained masses tend to zero. The inequality E<=(d+1)T gives the assertion for E. Consequently the convex functions -T_K^(1/d) and -E_K^(1/d), on K, vanish on its entire boundary. Testing boundary transport with them can therefore give equality without constraining any interior mark. Possible use of their convex extensions or limits does not alter this zero-trace fact.

## 2. A complete actual four-fiber example

Take n=d=2 and

    v0=(-1,-1), v1=(1,0), v2=(0,1),
    P={0,v0,v1,v2},  B=conv(v0,v1,v2).

Then B intersect Z^2=P. Indeed barycentric coordinates t0,t1,t2 give z_i=t_i-t0. If an integer coordinate is -1, then t0=1 and z=v0. Otherwise both coordinates are nonnegative integers with sum at most one, giving the other three listed points.

Let K be any full-dimensional triangle, of area V, with barycentric coordinates lambda0,lambda1,lambda2 and centroid g. Set C=B times K. Its mixed set is P times K and its mass is 4V. Define

    ell0(z)=-z1-z2,
    ell1(z)=2z1-z2,
    ell2(z)=2z2-z1,
    H_j={lambda_j(x)-1/3+ell_j(z)>=0}.

The three margins sum to zero, so these closed halfspaces cover all of ambient space. Each cap has one strict full outer fiber, two strict empty outer fibers, and a centroid vertex cap of fraction 4/9 at base zero. Hence

    Q=(13/9)V,  beta=Q/(4V)=13/36.                         (3)

The point Y=(0,g) actually has raw depth Q. To prove the all-normal lower bound, write any through-Y margin as a dot z+u dot (x-g). Its own trace has volume at least (4/9)V by ordinary centroid Grünbaum (or the independently proved energy/cap bound). On the three outer fibers, couple uniform triangle points X_j by their three cyclic barycentric permutations. They are uniform, sum to 3g, and the corresponding v_j sum to zero. At least one of the three coupled margins is nonnegative pointwise. Thus the total outer captured mass is at least V, including pure-integer normals and boundary equalities. Together these give (3).

The deepest point is unique. At any point not lying on all three displayed cap boundaries, one cap margin is positive because the margins sum to zero. A sufficiently small positive shift of that cap's threshold retains the point and strictly decreases its mass: the proper central section loses positive volume. A point on all three boundaries has lambda_j(x)=1/3-ell_j(z). Since ell_j(z) are integers and barycentric coordinates lie in [0,1], all ell_j(z) must be zero, forcing z=0 and x=g.

Thus Y is also the unique T-then-E selected point. All other fibers contain no actual globally deepest point. Nevertheless all their ordinary centroid marks have the same full retained mass and energy V.

All cap-body intersections away from base zero are strict, and the three central cuts are proper. The coarea section centroids are g and their unnormalized coarea masses agree. Hence the exact equal response weights are theta_j=1/3, with no facet-allocation ambiguity.

## 3. Exact source and target boundary laws, with one explicit coupling

Let eta be the sum of surface-length measures on the four fiber boundaries, carrying their continuous outward normals. Put

    W=(1/3)sum_j 1_Hj,
    dnu=(W/beta)deta=(12/13)sum_j1_Hj deta.                (4)

The coefficients in (4) have sum 36/13=1/beta, precisely the normalized stress scale. They retain the actual cap incidences.

Work on any fixed edge of K, of length L, with affine parameter r in [0,1]. On this edge the two nonzero barycentric coordinates are r and 1-r. Write U for uniform probability on [0,1], and U_mid for uniform probability on [1/3,2/3]. The boundary laws on this edge are

    nu at base 0 = L[(12/13)U+(4/13)U_mid],
    nu at each outer base = L(12/13)U,
    eta at each of the four bases = L U.                    (5)

Here the central density relative to length is 12/13 on the two outer thirds and 24/13 on the middle third, exactly as prescribed by (4).

The following positive componentwise construction is a single martingale coupling of (5).

* Send the 12/13 uniform component at each outer base identically to that base and parameter.
* From the central 12/13 uniform component, send 9/13 uniformly and identically to the central base, and 1/13 uniformly and identically to each outer base.
* For the central 4/13 middle-third component, write its input as r=(1+s)/3 with s uniform in [0,1]. Keep its target base zero and choose, with equal probabilities, the three target parameters (s+j)/3, j=0,1,2.

In the second step the total conditional target base mean is zero because v0+v1+v2=0; its continuous parameter is unchanged. In the third step the conditional mean parameter is (s+1)/3=r, and the mixture of the three thirds is uniform on [0,1]. Thus EVERY conditional physical mean is the actual input point. All targets stay on the same edge, so the continuous normal is preserved exactly.

The resulting target mass is 12/13+1/13=1 on each outer base, and 9/13+4/13=1 on the central base. Multiplying by L and repeating on all three edges proves all source and target marginals. Endpoints are surface-null; there is no hidden cap-boundary atom.

Consequently this is a full actual normal-preserving boundary martingale from the genuine critical trace stress nu to eta. It transports central boundary mass 3L/13 into the three fibers having NO deepest mark. Summing edges gives outgoing mass 3 sigma/13, where sigma is the perimeter of K.

This escape is not an artifact of the chosen coupling. The total central source mass is 16 sigma/13, while the central target mass is sigma. Therefore ANY coupling with these marginals sends at least 3 sigma/13 of the central source mass outside its base. The martingale condition is not needed for this lower bound.

The stress is genuinely nontrivial. For the convex base test Phi(z,x)=|z|^2,

    integral Phi d(eta-nu)=4 sigma/13>0.                (6)

For T and E of the common continuous triangle, both boundary traces are zero. Thus these two invariants have equality on every row of the displayed boundary coupling while no destination mark becomes deepest. Whole-fiber equality is already present in this product, so it cannot repair the missing depth implication by itself.

There is also an exact interior-mark calibration. Multiply this coupling by h_(K-g)(u), which is positive and constant along each retained normal. This preserves the row barycenters and normal preservation. The outward surface measure h_(K-g)(u)dS has total mass 2V and barycenter g: the divergence identities are

    integral_boundaryK (x-g) dot n dS=2V,
    integral_boundaryK x[(x-g) dot n]dS=2Vg.

Thus the outgoing 1/13-uniform component at EACH outer base has continuous mean precisely g after this legitimate weighting. Its actual destination interior mark is (v_j,g), with T=E=V, exactly the ordinary T/E values of Y. Yet none of those marks is deepest. This rules out inferring mixed deepestness even after this natural normal-weighted boundary-to-centroid averaging. It does not require the continuous triangle to be equilateral.

## 4. The strict-quota R4 upgrade

The already audited source `candidate b78a2eb10bd3783f` supplies a stronger arithmetic calibration. Its base is

    P=conv{(-4,-4),(4,0),(0,4)} intersect Z^2,

with 31 points and parity-class sizes 10,7,7,7. Every nonempty proper closed minor T satisfies

    |T|/31<k(T)/4,

with margin at least 1/124. Equal fiber volumes make these actual strict mass-count quotas. Its same canonical triangle caps have exact globally critical normalized mass beta=40/93. Full all-normal proof and independent audits are in `candidate de93c4f08837e128`, `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`, and `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`. That long all-normal certificate is used here as a proved dependency, not replaced by numerical evidence or rerun unnecessarily.

The deepest point is again uniquely (0,g), by the same strict cap-threshold argument and integer margins used in Section 2. Its T-then-E stratum is therefore a singleton.

The archived exact 144-edge certificate gives the complete normal-preserving martingale from nu=(W/beta)eta to eta. On each continuous facet the central source mass is

    (Gamma_2/beta)L=(31/30)L,

whereas its target mass is L. Hence EVERY such coupling must send at least L/30 from the deepest source fiber to other fibers. Across the whole boundary the mandatory outgoing mass is at least sigma/30.

For completeness, the existing finite certificate lifts to a full boundary coupling as follows. On each of the 93 base/third states, W is 1/3 or 2/3. Thus nu has density 31/40 or 31/20 relative to eta. Keep the common minimum of nu and eta identically. High states have remaining density 11/20=22/40, low states have target deficit 9/40. The archived positive rational matrix has row sums 22, column sums 9 and exact physical barycenters; divide it by 40 and apply the affine map (z,s)->(z,(r+s)/3) at every common r in [0,1]. Integrating r gives the required whole boundary coupling. This construction preserves the actual three-bit cap incidences entering W.

Independent short certificate rerun: `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_r4_facet_martingale_slab_recovery.py` gives **732 exact checks PASS**. Its count quotas, marginals, positivity and physical barycenters are all checked. The existing long all-normal certificate remains the source of genuine criticality.

Both examples are far above the OC target: respectively 13/36 and 40/93, against Gamma_2/4=1/9. The R4 example excludes using mere completeness, criticality and strict proper-minor count quotas to infer deepestness of stress destinations. It does not exclude a new argument that essentially uses the strict bad-depth premise or its stronger quantitative quotas.

## 5. What remains valid at a hypothetical attained bad minimum

The proved all-convex-potential stress gives normal-preserving martingale transport, actual support equality and affine moment balance. The T-then-E theorem gives whole-fiber translation rigidity only for barycentric relations BETWEEN ALREADY SELECTED deepest marks. It does not turn transported boundary points, or the conditional centroid of their outputs in another fiber, into selected deepest marks.

At a fixed actual body, selecting an interior deepest mark that maximizes T and then E is not a two-sided optimization over body erosions. Thus it does not impose equality in every convex-potential inequality. Even when an individual deformation has neutral primary first response, the exact nonlinear persistence of the deepest set remains a separate obligation before applying a secondary T/E response test.

Section 1 supplies a precise valid equality alternative: if additional reasoning forces equality for a separating convex potential whose relevant source points lie in its zero set, then transport stays in that zero set. If it forces equality for a strictly convex physical potential, transport is diagonal. Neither conclusion follows from the current signed-affine stress, or from the boundary-zero traces of T and E.

No assertion about mass exhaustion, a paying global center, or the numerical OC constant is made here.

## 6. Check of the translated-family endpoint

The short root note `candidate b5b06a687cb4f54a` passes an independent full read. Its endpoint is correct and useful: if an actual complete family consists of compatible translates c_p+K, any anchored inclusion forces c_p=sum lambda_i c_(p_i), since a compact body cannot contain a nontrivial translate of itself. Hence the convex hull of the center graph has exactly one point over every integer base.

Intersections of convex subsets of that graph hull meet the graph exactly when their projected intersection meets Z^n. Applying finite weighted Doignon to convex hulls of subsets of weight greater than (1-2^-n)W gives one actual graph center of halfspace weight at least W/2^n. Each centroid-containing continuous trace supplies Gamma_d of the common fiber. This proves Gamma_d M/2^n for the ENTIRE translated family, even when its center graph is not globally affine. Pure-integer normals capture the whole selected fibers and cause no issue.

For only one complete rigid subfamily J, the same proof pays its mass M_J. Separately paying several classes does not select one center paying their sum. Thus this exact endpoint does not bypass the destination/deepestness and mass-exhaustion gaps above.
